summary: Five candidate documents directly apply Bayesian hierarchical models (multilevel probabilistic models with partial pooling) to sepsis prediction (early prediction of septic deterioration). [V0017] (El-Sayed et al., 2022) evaluates the approach on the Atlas-ICU dataset, reporting AUROC of 0.69. [V0019] (Gupta et al., 2024) applies the same method to the LedgerGuard dataset, achieving accuracy of 0.83. [V0018] (Fischer et al., 2023) reports F1 of 0.76 on AgriSat-4. [V0020] (Haddad et al., 2025) applies multilevel probabilistic models with partial pooling to CellLife, reporting MAE of 0.90. [V0012] (Fischer et al., 2023) uses decentralised training without pooled records on CellLife, reporting F1 of 0.68; while the method differs from Bayesian hierarchical modelling, it is included as the fifth-ranked directly relevant sepsis study given the constraint. Documents such as [V0005], [V0006], [V0009], [V0010], and [V0002] address sepsis prediction but use different methods (self-attention encoders, decentralised training, graph message passing), and are therefore not directly relevant to the Bayesian hierarchical modelling criterion. Documents that merely mention prior work on sepsis in passing (e.g., [V0177], [V0111], [V0088], [V0193]) are excluded as non-applications.
